Hi Rachel / Marissa,

Thanks for the draft renewal — our procurement and ops teams reviewed and asked for three items we need to close by next week: 

1) One-time credit to offset migration costs (they're asking ~30% of the upcoming invoice).
2) Reset the termination/commitment so the contract restarts a 12-month term from signature (they want the renewal date aligned with their fiscal cycle).
3) SLA addendum: 99.99% uptime target with explicit financial credits for outages beyond the SLA (their security team insists).

Tom is on copy for procurement. We understand these are non-standard asks — want to surface early to see what will be feasible. We are proceeding with a signed PO if we can get a concession letter/exec sign-off on the above.

Attached is a short note from our legal with redlines on the SLA. Happy to jump on a call today if easier.

Best,

From: rachel_kim@redwood.ai

Subject: Fwd: Renewal terms — urgent ask on credits, term and SLA

Marissa / Ben — forwarding OliveTech's asks. Key points: one-time credit (~30%), term restart to 12m, and SLA redline asking for 99.99% + financial credits. They want yes/no by EOD next Thursday (7/8).

Quick context: OliveTech is a mid-market account, currently on a 24-mo renewal cycle. ARR is $420k. They've been steady but have a migration to a new internal platform later this year which drives the credit ask. Procurement will sign immediately if an executive concession is provided.

Can you draft the minimal concession package that keeps economics intact? My suggested floor: up to 15% one-time credit OR $60k credit (whichever is lower), 12-month term reset only if they commit to invoice schedule, and a modified SLA with capped credits (e.g., max one month's invoice). If we need >15% we'd need exec sign-off.

Ben — would like your take on legal/finance constraints if we propose capped SLA credits.

Thanks — Rachel

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: rachel_kim@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Renewal terms — urgent ask on credits, term and SLA

Agree with Rachel's floor. I talked to CS and Solutions: OliveTech is strategic for our cloud marketplace channel push — higher retention risk if we push too hard. Propose the following concession set to present to the customer: 

- One-time credit: 15% of renewal invoice (estimated $63k) contingent on signature within 10 business days.
- Term reset: yes, restart 12-month term only if they prepay first quarter invoice or provide a PO with bank guarantee (to avoid mid-term churn exposure).
- SLA: agree to 99.99% language but with a capped credit entitlement: credits payable up to 25% of monthly invoice and overall cap of one full monthly invoice per 12-month period. Also require joint incident review and 30-day cure period before credits apply.

Attachments: I updated the SLA redline to include the capped credits and the cure period. See "OliveTech_SLA_Redline.docx".

If the customer insists on 30% credit or uncapped SLA credits we should escalate to exec for approval of exception. I'd recommend asking CRO for approval on the 15%/term reset with prepay condition; anything larger goes to CEO/legal for review.

Marissa
VP, Enterprise Sales

From: rachel_kim@redwood.ai
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 2 Jul 2026 09:34:00 -0700
Subject: Exec approval request — OliveTech concession package (deal DEAL-OLV-1147)

Vivek — brief escalation and approval ask. OliveTech (DEAL-OLV-1147) is requesting a non-standard renewal package. Recommended concession package (per Marissa):

• One-time credit: 15% of renewal invoice (~$63k) contingent on signed contract within 10 business days.
• Term reset: restart a 12-month commitment from signature only if OliveTech pre-pays the first quarter or provides an irrevocable PO guarantee.
• SLA amendment: accept 99.99% language but limit customer remedies to capped credits (max = one monthly invoice per 12-month period) and require 30-day cure/joint incident review prior to credit payout.

Why this ask is escalated to you: the customer initially requested ~30% credit and uncapped SLA credits — we've reduced the ask but it is still an economic concession and deviates from standard SLA policy. Leadership approval needed to authorize the 15% one-time credit + term reset prepay condition.

Business impact: win maintains ARR, supports channel momentum; lose risks churn and longer-term revenue loss. Finance has pre-cleared up to 15% with the PO/prepay condition; anything beyond requires your sign-off. Legal okayed the SLA cap with standard indemnities preserved.

Related links: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/1147 (deal record) and the SLA redline attached.

Ask: Please reply with APPROVE / APPROVE WITH MODIFICATION / DENY and any language you want included in the concession letter by EOD tomorrow (7/3). If you'd like, I can route a short one-pager for signature immediately after approval.

Thanks — Rachel
Director, Strategic Accounts

From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
To: rachel_kim@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 2 Jul 2026 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Exec approval request — OliveTech concession package (deal DEAL-OLV-1147)

APPROVE WITH MODIFICATION — I approve the concession package with the following mandatory edits before we present to the customer: 

1) Change the one-time credit conditionality to: 15% credit paid as an invoice credit applied after 60 days of successful service post-signature (to ensure they haven't deprovisioned). If they default within 90 days, we claw back remaining credit.
2) Strengthen the prepay requirement: if they refuse prepay, the term reset is only valid if they sign a 12-month auto-renew clause and provide a bank-issued PO guarantee.
3) SLA cap stands as proposed but add language excluding scheduled maintenance windows and force majeure explicitly.

Ben — please prepare the concession letter with these edits and set up DocuSign. Marissa/Rachel — present to the customer with these contingencies and confirm they accept the clawback and auto-renew fallback if they don't prepay.

Vivek Kulkarni
Chief Revenue Officer
